messages:
Priya: Quick note from the ops + billing sync: I prototyped a small design for a cheap billing-memo layer to dedupe cost reports across retries/fanout. Sharing for feedback.
Connor: Thanks. High-level: what's the read/write pattern?
Priya: Writes are append-if-missing on canonical key (req:stage). Read is rare and bulk by stitcher. Two-tier: in-memory LRU for hot hits, durable store (Redis or RocksDB) for correctness.
Luis: Concern: tombstone churn if we keep tombstones to prevent late-arrival double counts. How long do we keep them?
Priya: Plan: tombstones for 24h beyond memo TTL. TTL baseline 1h. For enterprise tenants we bump to 7d memo + 3d tombstone. Tombstone entry is ~32 bytes.
Nina: How do we estimate storage / cost for Redis? we need a quick ops number.
Priya: Example calc: avg memo 100B + tombstone 32B. At steady QPS 20k with 1h TTL -> 20k*3600*(100B+32B) ~ 9.4GB. Add headroom for replication (~x2). We'll produce a sizing table in RFC.
Connor: Sampling strategy? For very high volume endpoints we might only memoize 1/N requests. Stitcher needs to account.
Priya: Right. We plan sampled flags: memoized=true/false + sample_ratio. Stitcher will compute billed_cost = sum(memoed_costs) + extrapolate(sum(nonmemoed_costs) * sample_ratio^{-1}). We'll include confidence intervals.
Luis: Extrapolation will affect invoices. Legal will want SLAs on accuracy. How do we present error?
Priya: We surface estimated error per-tenant and tier. Default tolerance 0.5% at P95; enterprise SLA can require 0% sampling (persist all memos) or signed acceptance of sampling error.
Nina: Operational failure modes: Redis partition -> potential overbilling if duplicates accepted, or underbilling if writes failed. What's our fallback?
Priya: Fallback 1: best-effort local memo + emit idempotency checksum in envelope. Fallback 2: feature-flag to turn memo off for that service and let stitcher fall back to idempotent checksum dedupe (higher false-positive risk). We'll also have a reconcile job that scans trace logs and repairs missing memos where possible.
Connor: Reconcile job could be heavy. What's the plan to bound its cost?
Priya: Reconcile runs at low priority, windowed per-tenant and per-time-range; uses sampling to detect systemic issues then triggers targeted backfills for affected request ranges only.
Luis: Metrics we should emit?
Priya: Proposed metrics: billing.memo_write_total, billing.memo_write_failures_total, billing.memo_setnx_collisions_total, billing.tombstone_creates_total, billing.memo_evictions_total, billing.reconcile_runs_total, billing.reconcile_repaired_count. Add tracing tags: billing.memoized, billing.memo_key, billing.memo_checksum.
Nina: Anything for envelope shape changes? we must avoid inflating kafka payloads.
Priya: We won't add full memo to envelope. Minimal envelope fields: memo_ref and checksum. Example: {request_id, tenant_id, stage, cost_delta, memo_ref, memo_checksum}. Stitcher fetches memo by memo_ref as needed.
Connor: Who will own the RFC + tests?
Priya: I'll draft RFC. Volunteers for perf sims: @Connor (simulate QPS/cost), @Luis (legal/accuracy assumptions).
telemetry-bot: feature flag rollout: billing-memo staging=true on 2026-03-20T02:00Z.
Priya: thanks all, I'll post RFC link when ready. Keep comments inline on the doc rather than here after that.
